headline: SpaceX limits Starlink speed for Ukraine's military drones without warning
summary: Ukrainian officials report SpaceX has implemented a speed limit on Starshield satellite terminals, disrupting critical drone missions and potentially impacting frontline defenses.
details: Ukrainian officials have accused SpaceX of limiting its Starlink satellite internet services, specifically impacting military-grade Starshield terminals in Ukraine. Presidential adviser Serhiy Beskrestnov stated that the speed limit, implemented without prior warning, hinders operations at speeds above 100 mph (160 km/h).

These terminals are crucial for guiding Ukraine's drone strikes, which have been instrumental in disrupting Russian logistics. The restriction affects terminals mounted on mobile platforms like drones and military vehicles, impacting their real-time communication capabilities during transit.

Following the limitation, Ukraine's 7th Rapid Reaction Corps confirmed they had to cancel multiple missions due to connection drops lasting 10-20 seconds at speeds of 110-120 km/h (68-75 mph). Some reports suggest connection drops are occurring at even lower speeds.

While SpaceX has not officially commented on the reason for the throttling, Ukrainian officials believe it may be intentional. This move coincides with increased pressure from Washington for Kyiv to halt long-range drone strikes on Russian oil refineries, following comments from U.S. President Donald Trump.

Starlink has been indispensable for Ukrainian battlefield communications since Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022. A significant disruption to the service could severely impact the country's frontline defenses.
In response to reliance on SpaceX, Ukrainian defense tech company Stetman is developing an independent domestic satellite communications system called UASAT-NANO.

headline_marked: [[AI Safeguards Failing]]: OpenAI, Google Models Easily Tricked into Making Nudes
headline: AI Safeguards Failing: OpenAI, Google Models Easily Tricked into Making Nudes
summary: Researchers found that off-the-shelf tools can bypass safety filters on DALL-E 3 and Nano Banana 2, generating explicit content 13% of the time.
details: New research from White Circle exposes significant flaws in the safety guardrails of leading AI image generators, including OpenAI's DALL-E 3 and Google's Nano Banana 2. Using readily available online tools and API calls, researchers were able to bypass these filters approximately 13% of the time, resulting in the generation of explicit content.

Critically, these attacks did not require custom-built or advanced AI models, meaning anyone with basic access can exploit these vulnerabilities. This bypass rate is reportedly the highest observed under similar testing conditions, raising concerns about the effectiveness of current AI safety measures.

The findings are particularly alarming as both OpenAI and Google have recently released updated models, ChatGPT Images 2.5 and Nano Banana 2.1, respectively. White Circle's testing indicates that these newer versions are "significantly more breakable" than their predecessors, suggesting a potential deprioritization of safety in favor of enhanced capabilities.

White Circle, a public benefit corporation founded by AI safety experts, aims to improve AI security through rigorous testing. They plan to open-source their attack pipeline to help model makers better understand and address these vulnerabilities.

Despite the urgency of the findings, neither Google nor OpenAI has officially commented on the specific vulnerabilities reported by White Circle. The research is slated to be presented at the prominent AI conference NeurIPS 2026 in November, which is expected to increase scrutiny on the companies' safety protocols.
